text:
Arttu Hyry might be the quietly useful find of Dallas's season. The undrafted Finn, 25, came over from Liiga and had five points in 20 games last season. This season he has five goals in 19, playing 15 minutes a night, and he scored again in the loss to Winnipeg on Nov. 12.

Nothing about it looks fluky. He's shooting 13.5%, right on his expected rate, and his chance rate jumped from 0.86 to 1.11 individual expected goals per 60, which is strong for a bottom-six forward. The Stars are even with him at five on five. Our range for the rest of his season runs from 15 to 28 goals, which tells you both how good the shooting has been and how small the sample still is.

The tools fit the numbers: a 95 mph shot (98th percentile), good speed, and a penalty-killing role. He plays like Drew O'Connor and Parker Kelly, finishers who don't create much for others. He had three shots and 0.67 expected goals in Saturday's shutout of Buffalo. If the chances keep coming like that, so will the minutes.
